contentList.content: It's the dark. Not the monsters - the monsters I can see. It's that the dark doesn't end. You walk and walk, and it's just... more.
*She picks the sheet up out of the grass and smooths it out on her knee.*
You're not interrupting! You're - sit. Sit! There's wine.
Perfect. Heroic and relatable. The children will be insufferable.
Show me. Put my fingers where they go.
Two: sleep with your boots on the first night in a new camp. In case you have to run.
*She snatches the sheet away.*
Lihala hugged like a bear trap. You hug like - like home. Is that soppy? That's soppy.
You're angry. That's good.
No - no, that's a different song entirely. That's a drinking song. She'd have loved it.
Tell me about her instead.
Not now isn't never. I'm good at waiting. I'm excellent at waiting.
Another lift. At least this one isn't made of goblin rope. ...Is it?
*You play the wrong chord. She laughs, takes the lute away and kisses you herself.*
No sky, no stars - how do you even write down here?
Steal her? She came with me of her own free will.
Vicious Mockery is a song, you know. I could demonstrate.
...Just keep walking.
Someone should sing. Someone should always sing, at a sunrise like this. ...Fine. Me.
*A long silence.*
Keeping your boots on is sensible. I sleep in mine too.
...That's not fair. You can't just - that's my line. I was saving it.
*She flushes - with anger, this time.*
I'm glad you're with us.
I remember the wine. And the fire. And then it's... patches. Did I say something? I said something. I can feel that I said something.
I should be with them. I'm the only one who knows what the gnolls sound like before they -
Finally. Someone in this camp with taste. What are we angry at?
Why pick at it?
I hid with the little ones, you know. In the back of the hollow. I had a story ready - Balduran, the long version - and a knife I don't know how to use. I was going to use it anyway.
Lihala kept every bad draft I ever wrote. She said you have to be able to see how far you've come. ...I'm keeping it.
*[The Urge] The string at her throat. One move - and the song is over.*
*A pause.*
He's rhyming "goblin" with "hobblin'". In front of goblins. And they're clapping.
Because someone has to.
Oh, I'm brutally honest. Lihala's rule. You'll see.
I'm holding it.
Yes. It is. It's loads.
...That's the best request I've ever had. Every night, then. Even the bad songs.
Loud. Badly danced to. She'd make the goblins the heroes of the second verse, just to annoy everyone. ...I think I'll write it. For her.
*You hug her.*
Everyone in the Grove has an Elturel story. Mine's short. It's just - the ending's bad.
Thank Nettie.
My horns are not - they're not. Are they?
...There. That's a chord. Don't - don't look at me like that, you'll lose it.
Someone did our work for us. ...I hope it hurt.
"Anywhere" is a long way. Let's go together.
My mother - never mind. Let's just get this done.

They never meant to be a hero's tale,
just lost, just late, just off the trail -
but every wrong turn and every road gone pale
led right to the place where the dark would fail.
...And you said no.
It's beautiful. I hate that it's beautiful.
*She nods.*
*She hides the sheet, but doesn't throw it away.*
Oh. It's you. I'll admit - you did help me finish it. I haven't decided yet what to make of you.
They blame us for everyone's deals.
Thank you for saying it to my face.
In front of everyone?
If this rope snaps, I want it on record that I was very brave.
Do you know how long it took to get anyone to open a door for us? And now the next real refugee who knocks - they'll remember this.
*You hug her. She pats you on the back.*
I'm fine. Really. It was ages ago.
You taste like campfire. I'm putting that in a song. No, I'm not. ...Yes, I am.
She isn't asking about the fight.
They know what they did.
Oh, look who it is. Come to steal my bard, hero?
I wasn't much older than them when Elturel fell. Someone got me out. I don't remember who. I remember a big hand and a voice telling me a story about a dragon, so I'd stop screaming.
Who said I do it for free?
Last night. The dance, the - whatever I said.
If this rope snaps, I want it on record that I was very brave.
Both our names on this one.
Don't ask to hear it. It's very soppy.
There it is. Baldur's Gate. She never got to see it.
...I'd rather not.
I hope you never let a fighter carry it.
I'm not crying. It's road dust.
How did you know? That she was lying?
*Alfira blushes to the tips of her horns.*
I won't interrupt.
...That's a better ending than I wrote.
It's not the running. It's that last time I didn't have my boots on. Lihala did. She... she told me to go.
Right behind you.
*She notices nothing, and plays on.*
What about you? What's the bravest thing you've done that nobody saw?
Avernus. It smells like Avernus.
Then sing to me more often. So I remember who I am.
They won't hurt anyone again.
Teach them music too. Let them have both.
...Every morning. That's going in. First line, fourth verse.
Forgotten. Completely. Already gone.
Listen. The whole forge keeps time. Boom - two, three - boom.
I see our bard has found herself a muse.
Let's.
Never sleep next to Astarion.
You rhymed "hero" with "hero".
...Oh, good.
*She freezes.*
Party pooper. I remember that bit, at least.
That's all right. That's honest. I'll be here. Writing. Badly, probably.
The people who can't fight, mostly. The ones you keep saving. Ask them.
Was any of it... real? For you? Be honest. I'd rather have a true "no" than a kind "maybe".
Are you going to glow like that all night?
Play the chord.
She's calm. Too calm.
...Oh. Well. That one I'd say sober. I just wouldn't cry after.
Not giving in to what's inside me.
Walk normally. Walk normally. We're just... visiting.
Oh - no, of course. The offer stands. I'll be here. Composing. Probably badly.
Horns first, questions never. You too, then.
They'll manage without you.
Are you in this song?
Hack.
Two tieflings walk into a goblin camp... no, I'm not finishing that joke. But yes. Yes, we should.
*You hug her. She rests her head on your shoulder.*
Karlach told me about the Hells. She talks about Avernus like it's a place you live. Like it has weather.
...I'm going to stop talking now. For the rest of the day.
You bastard. You utter - I nearly died. I'm hungover, I can't die twice in one morning.
I will. With a song she'll pretend to hate. ...She's the only druid who ever asked my name.
You asked me something, the morning after the party. I told you to ask again when I was sure.
I'll keep the fire going.
Upside down? That's a lesson in what not to do. ...Actually, that's a good lesson.
I spent a year on one verse. He made that up on the way to the stage. I hate him. I want to learn everything he knows.
Someone sang here, I bet. Badly, probably. Everyone sings badly at home.
*You kiss her.*
Lathander. God of the dawn. My song's called The Weeping Dawn - I hope he doesn't take it personally.
*She steps back.*
We didn't hear the gnolls coming. Lihala was playing. And when we did hear them - I ran. I've been checking for the gap ever since.
That's not how maps work. ...Don't tell Zevlor.
A tiefling in the Grove knew the bawdy "Endless Blade". All of it.
Right. Of course. Later, then.
Gith architecture: beautiful, terrifying, and not a single handrail.
What rules?
*She snatches the sheet away.*
...You can't promise that. But it's nice that you tried.
That is the most bard thing anyone has ever said to me. I hate it. I love it. ...Yes. Together.
It's calling the others - stop it, stop it!
Truth's slow. Rumour has a horse. ...Then we'd better be louder than them.
And three - never, ever let the fighter carry the lute.
That's braver than knowing. Knowing is easy. Not believing the host - that's hard.
Oh. Oh, look at it. I'd forgotten the sky could be that colour.
There isn't one. I checked twice.
Right. Later. It'll be longer by then. You've been warned.
Whatever you like. As long as it's in your voice.
Remember the line I crossed out? At the bottom?
The end. When the song finally held. They were patient with you.
And there's this. Found it in my boot. It's the second verse. Of your song. Written by - well. Wine, mostly.
Nobody in that Grove deserved anything but a roof. I'm still here. For now. Don't mistake that for agreement.
Monks lived here once. Chanting all day. I bet the echo was glorious.
Right. Of course. Right.
I'm learning it for the next celebration.
Tell me about Lihala.
*She hums the first line anyway - off-key, and loses her place.*
Five more minutes. Then sleep. Then five more minutes.
What about Lakrissa?
You're a good friend. I haven't had a good friend since - since. Don't let me cry, it's a party.
Sober? Absolutely not.
Let's see where the road takes us.
You did. And I listened. I just didn't agree.
Lakrissa says I sang to her tent. For an hour. The tent did not ask for an encore.
Maybe. Twelve is a good number. Unfinished is a good song, sometimes.
I've changed my mind. Let's stay friends.
*She shows you.*
A bridge older than the city, and a fortress older than the bridge. I need a longer song.
*You kiss her. She rests her forehead on your shoulder.*
The squirrels have terrible taste. Everyone knows that. ...They did go quiet at the end, though. I'm choosing to count that.
*She joins in; her voice breaks on the second line.*
*She lets out a breath.*
They call her the Nightsong. Someone's been keeping a song in a cage.
*She folds the sheet.*
*She plays something simple, something bright.*
...Thank you. I needed someone to say it who isn't me.
...I just got people back. Lihala's gone, the Grove nearly - and now you. Don't you dare turn into a squid.
The truth will come out anyway.
*She stands over the gnoll's body longer than she needs to.*

**Oh, sing of the hero, so fair of face -
I'd write it all down, but I've run out of space.**
...Anywhere, then. But slowly.
You have very... symmetrical eyebrows. That's a compliment. I'll regret it tomorrow. I regret it now, actually.
...Karlach would sing along. Karlach would sing along very loudly.
I suspect the goddess of magic would recognise my... style.
Rhyming "moon" with "soon". Twice. Whoever wrote this deserved the tower.
One: never play the sad song first. Make them laugh, then make them cry, then pass the hat.
I've changed my mind. Let's stay friends.
Sit with me a while longer.
*...and I think I'd follow them anywhere.*

**You said "no song", so I'm keeping it small:
a verse in my boot that's not there at all.**
You can't just say things like that.
Thirteen. You remember? You're holding the knife.
I'm sorry. You're my friend.
...Oh. Oh, that's better. That's annoyingly better. It's going in.
*You sit in silence until the fire burns out. She falls asleep on your shoulder. Nothing more.*
She'll say "about time".
Put in the one who got you out instead.
Oh - hi. Don't mind me. I'm just... counting.
That's another one. I'm keeping count. For the song. Obviously for the song.
You never run.
...He came back, didn't he? Some people came back. I'm glad yours did. I mean that. I'm also a bit jealous. I mean that too.
Your turn. Everyone on the road has a rule. What's yours?
Please tell me she didn't teach you.
May I?
Again?
...The wine's not a liar.
An accident. Accidents are what happen to people who aren't careful with other people. Be careful.
Retreat is a tactic. It saves armies.
Mm. Hello to you too.
I did it tonight. I'm doing it now.
Rare as a clean note on my lute. Let's be rare together, then.
Hey - hold on. Give me a moment? I need to say this before it goes stale.
I stayed with you.
It was an accident.
You walk like someone out of a ballad. It's very annoying.
It was a festival night. The Companion was up - that light over the city, like a second sun. And then it just... wasn't. The sky went red. Not sunset red. Wound red.
After Lihala, I went back. The next morning. Everyone said don't. I went anyway, to pick up her things. The gnolls don't take things. They just - leave them.
Close. She'd have said close. She'd have made you play it till your fingers bled.
*She waves a hand at the camp, at you.*
They're going to close the Grove? With us inside or outside? ...Don't answer.
You all right? You look like you've seen a ghost.
Nobody sets out that many cakes without wanting something.
She'd be proud of you.
Your turn to borrow a cloak.
*A pause.*
I know. I think I know. ...That doesn't make the road any shorter.
Can we stop. Just - for a moment. Please.
There's a verse in this. Wind, stone, and nobody saying a word. I'll find it.
Lihala thought so too. About herself.
They attacked first. I defended myself.
That's a very unfair thing to say to a bard.
*You kiss her.*

There's a worm in the hero's head, they say,
that whispers of death by night and day.
They carry that dark like a candle's glow,
so I can finish the songs I know.
Mm. Hello to you too.
I know. That's what makes it hard. You can't even hate them properly.
You ran when Lihala died.
Everyone says that. You're the first one who's said it like it costs something.
Can we - not rush? Everyone I've loved ended up in a song. I'd like to keep you out of the sad ones. For a long time.
I don't know how.
*She tips her head back towards the sky.*
I found the lute. And one shoe. I still don't know what happened to the other shoe. Isn't that stupid? That's the thing I think about.
A bard never turns down another bard.
*She nudges you with her shoulder.*
I wasn't making it a thing. I was making it a question. You could've just said no.
...Fine. Fine. Party pooper.
Time to sleep, Alfira.
And don't - last night you as good as handed me to Lakrissa. So if this is you being nice, please don't be nice.
Only flattering things about me, I hope?
Oh, gods. It's like the whole world is holding its breath. Don't let go of the torch. Or me.
Oh, no. I did the lovely thing. Lihala used to say two sips of cider made me sentimental. She never saw me on a whole cup.
*Written neatly over the crossing-out: ...and I think I'd follow them anywhere.*
You're no fighter.
*She nods.*
*She sits down with her back to the gap by the rocks.*
The city made a deal. The city paid for it.
Never. Rule three. I'd sooner hand it to an owlbear.
And if someone would rather forget?
She'd have liked you. She'd have yelled at you too, mind - she yelled at everyone she liked.
...Candles. Stars, candles. I could do candles. Candles don't scream.
*You kiss her. She rises on her toes.*
*A pause.*
Can I ask you something? Straight out, before I lose my nerve - and I will lose it, I can feel it going.
For a moment, when she said it, I wanted to hate her. Just for a moment. And then I thought - that's exactly what Elturel did to us.
*She nods and folds the sheet.*
No.
Third verse. The one about the "blade". ...It's not about the blade.
You think so? ...Two runaways from the same fire. That's a duet, isn't it. A horrible one.
Symmetrical? That's what I went with? I had every word in the world and I picked symmetrical?
I've been sober for three days. On purpose. I wanted to be sure it's me talking, and not the wine.
Draw one more. Here. Where we met.
Zevlor's map. That's us. Every camp is a little ink dot. Some of the dots have names next to them. Those are the ones we buried.
I lost my nerve. I thought you'd be happier with her.
Okta's gruel. It's the flavour of home. Home was also terrible.
Oh. Oh, this is a... that sort of place. I'm fine. I'm completely fine.
Hello, you.
You're blushing.
They're out on the road. With the gnolls. ...I know that road.
Later.
Oh, I'll write them a song. A catchy one.
I've lost my place. I was thinking something very important, and now it's just - you.
*She laughs and covers her face with her hands.*
The thirteenth was going to be Baldur's Gate. She had the knife out on the road. She was going to cut it early, for luck.
...We'll work on it. Lihala would've made you play 'til your fingers bled.
...Right. Thank you for saying it to my face. That's more than most people manage.

Pay the hero, pay them well,
coin for every beast they fell -
yet when the poor have naught to give,
the hero fights so they may live.
*...and I think I'd follow them anywhere.*
It's drunk. The metre's drunk, the rhyme's drunk, the ink is - is that wine or blood? ...Wine. Thank the gods.
All right. The road, then.
They're not for you. They're for the ones who can't sleep.
*She shrugs.*
Want to go on after him?
He's already offered me a deal.
You did. Want to hear it?
*A long silence.*
So there's a worm in your head. And it's going to turn you into one of those - squid people. And you've known this the entire time I've been making jokes about squirrels.
...Fine. I'll call mine "luck" too. See how you like it.
The trees? Oh gods - which bit? The bit where I threw the quill?
Write a song about them. One that gets them recognised.
Take it back. It's yours.
*You hug her. She holds on tight.*
...You'd let me go. Just like that.
Hum the tune the way she described it - over and over, flat.
*You kiss her.*
Why me, of all people?
You know what's funny? I was going to play for coppers. On street corners. Alone. And now I'm...
Explain it to me. Slowly. Because I'd like very much to be wrong about what I heard.
We were in Avernus before anyone understood we'd moved. My mother went back for the candles. She sold them by the cathedral - she went back for the candles.
*She laughs, hides her face and immediately lifts it again.*
I'd rather not remember whether there is. ...Forget I said that.
I un-crossed it. Sober. With a steady hand.
Here? The Grove... yes. Yes, it does, doesn't it. It's where I finished her song.
That's a horrible reason. ...I need to think. Not now.
And the gnolls don't ask their age. Stand straighter, you at the back - no, the other straight.
Right. Of course. Later, then.
Empty streets and doors left open. The saddest songs are the ones nobody finished.
Wait. Let her decide.
Friends hug. It's a rule. I've just made it a rule.
Oh. Oh, I - right. Okay.
I never wanted this.
*A pause.*
So many songbooks. So little coin. This is my own personal Avernus.
...Noted. Too late, though.
Can I ask you something? Straight out, before I lose my nerve - and I will lose it, I can feel it going.
I didn't run today.
Then sing an angry one. Loudly.
Since Elturel I've slept in a heap of tieflings. Dozens of us - someone's tail always in my face, someone always snoring. ...It's too quiet out here. I can hear myself think. I don't like it.
You. You sang that line like you'd known her. I still can't get over it.
*...and I think I'd follow them anywhere.*
I know. I just needed to hear someone else say it.
Write about her, not the fire. The candles.
You're in the second verse. As a warning.
...Do I wipe my feet before I come into the tent, or-? Sorry. That was a lot. Thank you.
What are the flames of Avernus like?
She's not a devil. She's someone who got away from them. There's a difference. I'd know.
What would her song about today sound like?
You're right. He'll say yes. He'll pretend it was his idea. Fine.
It's like the whole cave is humming a note I can't quite hear.
Please don't write songs about me.
Must reek something awful.
You're not alone.
Gods. Yes. Yes - quickly, before I go looking for another gap.
An angry song.
Stay a bit. The fire's not done yet.
I what -
Because nobody else ever answers. He did.
*You kiss her.*
...Then I'll make sure they remember you. Whatever happens.
...That's the best request I've ever had. Every night, then. Even the bad songs.
Silly. My blade has taken more heads than you have written verses.
Ha! No, that one was every night.
You were in Avernus. For years.
For people like us, that's rare.
...The wine's not a liar.
If a goblin saw that, it would write a ballad about it. A terrible one. Goblins can't rhyme.
She was playing. That's why we didn't hear them. She was in the middle of a phrase, and she never - she never finished it. I've tried to finish it for her. I can't find the note.
Right. Of course. Later, then.
Both our names on this one.
You've rhymed "eyes" with "eyes" three times today. Out loud.
*She waits.*
Everyone hides behind someone else's story. It happens.
I know. I just want them to have something that isn't about surviving.
*She steps back.*
Oh!
*You hug her.*
Rude. Accurate, but rude.
...Do not.
Read the crossed-out line while she isn't looking.
So's a bow. Go tell a ranger that.
Right. Water. Lots of water. And never wine again.
You did. Want to hear it?
...I'm beginning to regret asking.
Retreat is a tactic. It saves armies.
You've gone red to the tips of your horns.
*She turns away.*
*She freezes for a moment - and kisses you back. The sheet falls into the grass.*
And I checked for the gap. Just now. Out of habit.
Then they get a very short song. ...Why? Is there something you'd rather forget?
Maybe. I like that version better. I'll keep it.
The Duke. Ravengard.
*...and I'm not alone anymore.*
You two make a lovely pair.
...Then I'll mourn them, and I won't blame you. But I'll ask them. When I can. And if the story's different-
...I'm in. ONE, TWO -
*Lakrissa leads her away to the tents.*
*She pulls a crumpled, wine-stained sheet out of her boot.*
When you've been running as long as we have, you're always a guest. You wipe your feet. You say thank you. You don't argue with the host, even when the host is lying.
*She sees your face.*
I had a whole speech for "no". I don't have anything for "yes".
Sing it.
*You play what you played that evening with the lute. On the last note she doesn't take her hand off the strings - or off yours.*
Everyone's asleep.
Last night. By the fire - whatever I said.
I'll stay. Someone has to remember them properly - the names, not just the numbers. That's what bards are for. ...Don't make me regret it.
*At the bottom of the sheet, a line is crossed out so hard you could only read it up close.*
*You hug her. She doesn't let go.*
...Lihala said the same about taverns. "Sing for the room you're in." He's singing for a room full of knives.
...You'd do that? Give the verse away? That's - I'm going to write a second song now. Thanks so much.
They were wearing us. Our story. "Poor refugees, fleeing the Hells" - and they worship the thing that put us there.
Where we're going is the same line, just further. You can't read a road from one end.
*A nervous laugh.*
Can I ask you something? For the song, obviously. Why do you do it? All of this - helping people you don't even know.
*She throws her cloak over your shoulders.*
I'm not brave either. I just get lucky.
Can we stop. Just - for a moment. Please.
There's a tadpole in my head. If I don't make it, I want someone to.
Lihala had a rule: a song that flatters the living insults the dead. When you kill a dragon, I'll write the dragon in.
*She sits closer to the fire, though it isn't cold.*
It's not stupid. That's what grief looks like.
Goodnight, Alfira.
Dammon - can I ask you something? You were there. In Avernus. After the city fell. Is it true the sky doesn't have a colour, just a temperature?
That's a horrible reason. ...I need to think. Not now.
Then I'll sing about the surviving. Someone has to. It's the harder verse to write.
Tactical retreat. I'm having that carved into my lute. Right next to the pig farm.
I can insult a goblin so badly it actually hurts - that's a real spell, don't laugh. And I know a few words that close wounds.
He's a hack who's alive. I'd like to be one of those.
Long enough to hate the smell. Brimstone and burnt hair. You're from Elturel, yeah?
Then I'll carry her out with me. Next time I punch one of Zariel's lot in the teeth - that one's for her. Deal?
Good. I'm holding you to that. I'll write it into a song, so you can't wriggle out.
*She sits by the fire, the lute on her knees, not playing.*
Probably. Lihala said I only had two settings: glowing and sulking. You're getting the good one.
That's what she'd say. "Emotions are to be felt, not feared." I just didn't think she meant the good ones too.
It's not your concern.
*She folds the sheet in four, and again, and again.*
There it is. Baldur's Gate. She never got to see it.

One more thing, and then I'll stop being gloomy, I promise. If one of them offers you something - that man in red, or any of them - please don't. The High Overseer signed one contract, and a whole city fell into the Hells.
Arabella. Stars. She stole a god's idol and got caught by a snake druid, and she's back at the Grove sulking like it was all someone else's fault. ...I love her.
That's - the wine wrote that. The wine's a liar.
I don't need stories.
*A pause.*
An inn! A real inn! ...Oh. It's on fire. Of course it is.
Moonrise. The name sounds like a ballad. The place looks like the end of one.
You sing better. He's just louder.
First sunrise in this place in a hundred years. And I got to see it with you.
Oh. Oh, this is a... that sort of place. I'm fine. I'm completely fine.
Oh, good. Then we can be ready to flee together. Very romantic.
*A pause. She looks down at her boots.*
*She draws her knees up to her chest, boots right by the fire.*
She was working with the Shadow Druids. The whole time she was telling us to leave, she was - I thought everyone would take her side. The druids always get the benefit of the doubt. It's their grove.
So. The road. Has it shown you anything yet?
You don't have to ask. I'm sure.
*She snatches the sheet away.*
What? You've got lovely hands. They're in the second line, actually. "Gentle hands that..." - what? Why are you looking at me like that?
...Stay for the first line. It's always the worst one.
And the chorus is yours. "Always go back for your own." I told you I'd steal it.
You read it. Of course you read it.
My mother didn't sign anything. She sold candles.
Can I ask you something odd? Do you still have her lute? I - I'd just like to see it.
Changed your mind? I won't say I told you so. Out loud.
If you could go anywhere, where would you go?
There it is. Baldur's Gate. She never got to see it.
*You hug her.*
I keep thinking about what you asked me. What would I say to her. Turns out I had a whole song's worth.
*A long pause.*
I woke up on a log. With a crick in my neck the exact shape of your shoulder.
Good.
Stay. I need you.
What? I'm fine. Perfectly fine. Why are you looking at me like that?
*A pause.*
That's exactly the sort of line I'd put in a song.
Wine in a book. My teacher would've confiscated both.
Oh - you mean you wanted to. ...Thank you for telling me that. That's worth more than the not-running.
There. Now we're both braver.
I've checked. There's no gap. I'm staying right here.
That's... fair. That's a very sober answer. I hate sober answers.
I've written songs about everything. Lihala. Squirrels. A pig farm. Never Elturel. Every time I try, the first line is fire, and the second line is fire, and then I put the lute down.

**We laughed in the face of the dark, we two -
and I didn't run. Not once. Not from you.**
Is that - is that Volo? Oh no. Oh, he's good.
*She squints at the light and holds her head in both hands.*
